title: Amplitude-aware burst fuzz and kernel sampler + burst-level quantile reporter
author: Diego Marquez
description:
Motivation: We frequently see production microbursts with varying amplitude (requests per second per tenant) that expose different kernel hotspots and scheduler contention compared to steady-state or single-amplitude bursts. Existing synthesizers in the benchlab cover sequence mix and temporal bursts but do not explicitly model amplitude variation across short epochs. This PR introduces an amplitude-aware burst fuzz workload generator and a lightweight kernel sampler that captures per-burst kernel execution profiles. The goal is to provide a representative, easy-to-run harness that surfaces scheduling regressions and kernel hotspots that only appear when burst amplitude varies within an epoch.

What this change does: Adds two new components under benchlab/runner: (1) amplitude_burst_fuzzer: a workload runner that generates epochs of bursts where each epoch has randomized amplitude envelopes (triangular, plateau, spike) with configurable intra- and inter-epoch jitter, sequence-length distributions, and optional KV-cache priming. (2) kernel_sampler: a synchronous sampler that inserts short trace probes to collect per-kernel aggregated metrics (time, samples, p95, p99) tied to burst ids and relative amplitude. Also adds burst_level_reporter: post-run pipeline that aggregates token-level latency into burst-aligned quantiles and amplitude histograms and produces a small JSON summary and a flamepoint CSV for interactive flamegraphs.

Checklist implemented: - [x] amplitude_burst_fuzzer CLI and Python API with configurable profiles and JSON config files - [x] kernel_sampler lightweight probe using existing benchlab tracing hooks (no runtime-internal changes) - [x] burst_level_reporter that emits per-epoch p50/p95/p99 + amplitude histogram and kernel flamepoint CSV - [x] unit + integration tests (fast-mode) and a longer local smoke test script - [x] docs/quickstart example and a README describing recommended knobs for reproducing production bursts - [x] CI jobs added to run linter, unit tests, and short bench smoke on PRs

How to run locally: 1) pip install -e benchlab 2) python -m benchlab.runner.amplitude_burst_fuzzer --config examples/amplitude_profiles/spike_plateau.json --out /tmp/run.json --sample-kernel true 3) python -m benchlab.reporters.burst_level_reporter --input /tmp/run.json --out /tmp/summary.json --flame /tmp/flamepoints.csv

Key design notes: - The fuzzer intentionally correlates amplitude envelopes with sequence-length distributions to reproduce real-world patterns where long requests cluster during high-amplitude periods. - kernel_sampler samples at burst boundaries and during peak windows to avoid excessive overhead; sampling rate is configurable. - Reporter keeps output compact (one JSON per run + CSV flamepoints) so it can be archived in S3 and consumed by existing dashboarding scripts.

Observations from internal runs: On our 8-GPU cluster profile, a mixed amplitude profile increased the p99 of token generation by ~18% compared to a static amplitude run with the same total QPS, and kernel_sampler identified a single attention kernel path that accounted for 42% of added tail time during spikes. These findings are recorded in the example run outputs included in this PR.

Related: ENG-2741 (burst analysis), ENG-3110 (kernel hotpath triage).

review_thread: Aisha Patel: Can you add a guard so sampling is disabled for runs where total qps < 1? Sampling caused flakiness in small CI runs.
Diego Marquez: Good catch — added a guard and a unit test (see fix commit).
Ethan Cole: Reviewed reporter output format. Suggest including burst_id and peak_amplitude in CSV header for easier joining.
Diego Marquez: Updated CSV header and added note in docs. Also included a short example of joining flamepoints with bursts in the README.
Maya Chen: Smoke CI ran but one test intermittently hit the RNG edge case for triangular envelopes; added deterministic seed in tests. Approved after fixes.
Aisha Patel: LGTM pending addressing minor doc language nit (done). Approved and merged.

release_notes: Adds amplitude-aware burst fuzz workload, lightweight per-burst kernel sampler, and a burst-level quantile reporter. Useful for surfacing kernel hotspots and scheduler regressions that appear only under variable-amplitude bursts.
notes_for_qa: QA: run examples/amplitude_profiles/spike_plateau.json in local CI mode and confirm reporter JSON contains burst-level p50/p95/p99 and flamepoints CSV can be loaded into flamegraph tool. Check that sampler overhead is <5% in short smoke runs.
